item.title: Seshadri constants of singular loci of line arrangements with at most twelve lines
item.description: arXiv:2611.03797v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let ${\mathcal L}$ be an arrangement of $d$ lines in the complex projective plane and let $Z={\operatorname{Sing}}({\mathcal L})$. A question of Pokora asks whether the multipoint Seshadri constant of ${\mathcal O}_{\mathbb{P}^2}(1)$ at $Z$ is always computed by a line of the arrangement containing the largest number of points of $Z$. We prove that the answer is affirmative for every arrangement of at most twelve lines. The proof uses a B\'ezout-type covering criterion, elementary restrictions on the intersection lattice, and a detailed analysis of the two extremal combinatorial types that can occur for twelve lines. One type is the Hesse arrangement; it is handled using a net of quartics through its twelve double points. The other type would yield a uniquely determined incidence structure on thirteen lines. We show that this incidence structure is not realizable over any field.
item.dc:creator: Marcin Dumnicki, {\L}ucja Farnik, Krishna Hanumanthu, Brian Harbourne, Piotr Pokora, Joaquim Ro\'e, Halszka Tutaj-Gasi\'nska

item.title: Min-plus Bruhat decomposition
item.description: arXiv:2611.03896v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study min-plus Bruhat cells $B_{trop}^{(n)} \odot p\odot B_{trop}^{(n)}$, where $B_{trop}^{(n)}$ denotes the set of all upper-triangular matrices over $\RR \cup \{\infty\}$, and $p$ is a permutation. It is proved that $\dim (B_{trop}^{(n)} \odot p \odot B_{trop}^{(n)})= \frac{n(n+1)}{2} + l(p)$, where $l(p)$ is the length of $p$ in Coxeter generators. Also we provide an explicit description of the cell $B_{trop}^{(n)}(\RR) \odot p_0\odot B_{trop}^{(n)}(\RR)$ (up to a subset of dimension less than $n^2$) for the highest in Bruhat order permutation $p_0$. Finally, it is shown that for a tropically non-singular matrix $A$ for at most one permutation $p_A$ it can hold $A\in B_{trop}^{(n)}\odot p_A\odot B_{trop}^{(n)}$.
item.dc:creator: Dima Grigoriev

item.title: D-equivalence conjecture for hyperk\"ahler varieties of generalized Kummer type
item.description: arXiv:2611.04118v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that birationally equivalent hyperk\"ahler varieties of generalized Kummer type are derived equivalent, confirming the D-equivalence conjecture in this case. Combined with recent results of other authors, this settles the conjecture for all known deformation types of hyperk\"ahler varieties. The kernel is built from an equivariant Fourier-Mukai kernel on the sum-zero loci of powers of an abelian surface. We deform it along diagonal twistor paths, using the hyperholomorphic endomorphism algebra. Comparing wall hyperplanes gives a common twisted derived category for two adjacent birational models, and a finite sequence of wall crossings then gives the equivalence.
item.dc:creator: Will Donovan, Chengxi Wang, Nantao Zhang

item.title: Global vector fields and the automorphism group of regular semisimple Hessenberg varieties
item.description: arXiv:2611.04130v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a connected regular semisimple Hessenberg variety other than the full flag variety, we prove that the identity component of its automorphism group is an algebraic torus. The argument uses equivariant local coordinates and weight-homogeneous coefficient functions of vector fields.
item.dc:creator: Mikiya Masuda, Takashi Sato, Haozhi Zeng

item.title: Admissible extremal rays and the anticanonical minimal model program
item.description: arXiv:2611.04145v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop an anticanonical minimal model program for projective $\mathbb{Q}$-factorial klt pairs $(X,\Delta)$ such that $-(K_{X}+\Delta)$ is pseudoeffective. We first prove the cone and contraction theorems for potentially klt triples and establish the existence of flips for such triples. Using these results, we introduce the notion of admissible extremal rays and show that $(K_{X}+\Delta)$-positive admissible extremal rays are precisely the rays that are to be contracted by $-(K_{X}+\Delta)$-MMP. The elementary MMP steps associated to such admissible rays preserve klt singularities. For potentially klt pairs $(X,\Delta)$ with $\mathbb{Q}$-divisors $\Delta$, we prove that every $(K_{X}+\Delta)$-positive extremal ray is admissible and obtain a cone theorem for the $(K_{X}+\Delta)$-positive part of the Mori cone. Assuming termination of the anticanonical minimal model program, we establish a dichotomy: potentially klt pairs admit anticanonical minimal models, whereas non-potentially klt pairs admit non-admissible models.
item.dc:creator: Sung Rak Choi, Sungwook Jang, Dae-Won Lee

item.title: A Bubble Compactification of KSBA Moduli Space of Surfaces of General Type
item.description: arXiv:2611.04154v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct a bubble-tree enhancement of the KSBA moduli space of surfaces of general type using index-one-cover Deligne--Mumford stacks. The construction is inspired by bubbling phenomena for K\"ahler--Einstein metrics. Non-klt semi-log-canonical singularities are replaced by admissible simple-normal-crossing configurations: the cusp and degenerate-cusp components are rational, while the simple-elliptic case also contains elliptic ruled components. A key feature is that the construction avoids lci covers. We construct the moduli stack of polarized bubble-tree index-one-cover Deligne-Mumford stacks. The stack is in general not separated, and we construct its underlying separated algebraic space. We also construct the moduli stack of bubble-tree index-one-cover Deligne-Mumford stacks with labeled sections that record algebraic bubbling centers and compare it with the pointed metric bubble tree. The labeled sections determine a numerical class whose stability proves the separatedness of the moduli stack. We establish a perfect obstruction theory and a virtual fundamental class on the bubble-tree moduli stacks. This provides a novel and geometric pathway to prove the existence of a virtual fundamental class on the original KSBA moduli space, thus offering a new approach to a conjecture of Donaldson. We expect that parts of the construction extend to higher dimensions.
item.dc:creator: Yunfeng Jiang

item.title: Conjecture B for $X_{10}$ and its genus-two mirror
item.description: arXiv:2611.04293v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove Conjecture B of Akhtar--Coates--Corti--Heuberger--Kasprzyk--Oneto--Petracci--Prince--Tveiten unconditionally for the normalized family of maximally mutable Laurent polynomials with prescribed $T$-binomial edge coefficients associated with the degree-10 orbifold del Pezzo hypersurface $X_{10}\subset\mathbb{P}(1,2,3,5)$. An explicit $S$-extended quantum-period calculation determines the affine mirror map $\lambda=a-346$ and proves that the regularized quantum period equals the classical period as a formal power series throughout the family.
item.dc:creator: Alex Junior Gomez Saltachin

item.title: Canonical Projectivization of Algebraic Varieties in Characteristic Zero
item.description: arXiv:2611.04314v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct a canonical projectivization of every smooth proper algebraic variety $X$ in characteristic zero. Once a principalization procedure is fixed, the construction gives a finite sequence of blowups in smooth centers with smooth projective endpoint, natural under semilinear isomorphisms and preserving the quasi-projective core, the intersection of all maximal quasi-projective open subsets. At each stage we select finitely many ideals near the generic points of the image in $X$ of the boundary of a maximal quasi-projective open. Principalizing their product strictly lowers the dimension of that image. The selection is defined intrinsically, without a polarization or a chosen projective modification; a Hilbert scheme argument proves its finiteness. Naturality embeds the automorphism group in that of a smooth projective variety of the same dimension. We then extend the construction to smooth proper integral algebraic spaces, obtaining canonical projectivizations of all compact connected Moishezon manifolds.
item.dc:creator: Parsa Bakhtary

item.title: Algebraicity, Hodge Gradings, and the Geometry of Period Images
item.description: arXiv:2611.04471v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove the algebraicity of period images in arithmetic quotients without using o-minimality. The proof uses infinitesimal neighborhoods and formal algebraization to recover the images and the maps from their algebraic sources. Hodge positivity and an algebraic ampleness criterion yield the Griffiths polarization and quasi-projectivity. For lifted images, we construct Stein neighborhoods and holomorphic matrix realizations of the Hodge filtration. On closed horizontal subspaces, we bound canonical Bergman density below by the Hodge volume form. We compare the Bergman and Griffiths--Schmid metrics near one-parameter boundaries with nontrivial unipotent monodromy and nondegenerate graded period maps, and in all directions near general one- and two-node quintic threefolds. A period surface arising from abelian threefolds shows that the upper metric comparison fails in general.
item.dc:creator: Kefeng Liu, Yang Shen

item.title: Fat base schemes and unexpected hypersurfaces of type $(d+k,d)$
item.description: arXiv:2611.04564v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study hypersurfaces of degree $d+k$ containing a prescribed zero-dimensional fat point scheme $Z\subset\mathbb{P}^n$ and having multiplicity at least $d$ along a general codimension-two linear subspace. We associate with this interpolation problem a vector bundle on $\mathbb{P}^1$ whose splitting type determines the dimensions of all linear systems of type $(d+k,d)$. For a fat point of multiplicity $m$, we determine the exact number of conditions detected by this bundle and introduce the corresponding effective length. This leads to an excess formula separating the contributions of the splitting type, the part of the fat structure invisible to degree-$k$ fibrewise sections, and the Hilbert-function defect of the fixed scheme. We also prove a truncation theorem showing that multiplicities larger than $k$ contribute only a uniform twist of the bundle and, geometrically, fixed hyperplane components. Finally, we exhibit explicit planar and three-dimensional examples showing that genuinely unexpected phenomena persist for nonreduced fixed base schemes, including geometrically irreducible unexpected hypersurfaces.
item.dc:creator: Grzegorz Malara

item.title: K3 Categories and Mukai Homomorphisms for Debarre-Voisin Varieties
item.description: arXiv:2611.04602v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $M=X_6^\sigma$ be a smooth Debarre-Voisin hyperk\"ahler fourfold and $X=X_3^\sigma$ the associated smooth hyperplane section of $\operatorname{Gr}(3,10)$. Using the incidence correspondence between $X$ and $M$, we construct a family $\mathcal E$ of objects in the Kuznetsov component $\operatorname{Ku}(X)$. We write $v$ for the common Mukai vector of its fibers. We prove that the associated Mukai homomorphism \[ \Theta_{\mathcal E}|_{v^\perp}\colon v^\perp\xrightarrow{\sim}H^2(M,\mathbb Z) \] is an integral Hodge isometry and explicitly determine the inverse image of the Pl\"ucker polarization. For a very general point of the trivector divisor corresponding to discriminant $24$, we also construct an integral Hodge isometry between the full Mukai lattices of $\operatorname{Ku}(X)$ and the associated twisted K3 surface.
item.dc:creator: Ryo Akazawa

item.title: Isolated symplectic singularities admitting symplectic resolutions
item.description: arXiv:2611.04630v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give a proof that an isolated algebraic symplectic singularity of dimension $2n\ge 4$ admitting a projective symplectic resolution is analytically isomorphic to the minimal nilpotent orbit closure in $\mathfrak{sl}_{n+1}$ at the origin.
item.dc:creator: Duo Li, Yanjie Li

item.title: Local resolution of the second log-Fitting ideal
item.description: arXiv:2611.04723v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Logarithmic Fitting ideals encode the complexity of the corresponding morphisms in a natural and intrinsic way, and their principalisation offers a new perspective on problems such as the resolution of cotangent sheaves and the monomialisation of morphisms. In this paper, we give a local resolution theorem for log-rank adapted morphisms: after finite sequences of smooth local blow-ups, the first two log-Fitting ideals \mathcal{F}\_{n--1}(\sigma) and \mathcal{F}\_{n--2}(\sigma) become principal monomial ideals.
item.dc:creator: Yueting Jiang (UPCit{\'e}, IMJ-PRG)

item.title: Pushforwards of lc pairs under morphisms to abelian varieties
item.description: arXiv:2611.04801v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $f$ be a morphism from a log canonical pair $(X,\Delta)$ to an abelian variety $A$ and $D\sim_{\mathbb Q}m(K_X+\Delta)$ a Cartier divisor on $X$ with $m>1$ a rational number. We prove that $f_*\mathcal{O}_X(D)$ is globally generated after pullback by an isogeny. Our methods involve birational geometry, mixed Hodge modules and singular Hermitian metrics with the minimal extension property. Moreover, we provide simple counterexamples where the above result fails for plt pairs when $m=1$ and where the existence of Chen--Jiang decompositions fails for plt pairs for any $m\ge1$.
item.dc:creator: Fanjun Meng

item.title: Enumerative geometry of conics and double covers on projective complete intersections
item.description: arXiv:2611.04837v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We compare genus zero degree two Gromov--Witten invariants with the number of embedded conics on general projective complete intersections whose conic space has expected dimension zero. Their difference comes from double covers of lines. We compute this contribution as an integral of Chern classes over the Fano scheme of lines, using an explicit obstruction bundle on the compactified space of double covers.
item.dc:creator: Dang Tuan Hiep, Ha Thi Thao Tram

item.title: Derived Equivalences for Terminal Threefold Flops via Local Index-One Covering Models
item.description: arXiv:2611.04844v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Inspired by the quadratic involutions of Corti-Pukhlikov-Reid and Gavin Brown's description of hypersurface flips via toric GIT, we apply similar symmetries to local covering models of terminal threefold flops. We recover the derived equivalence of their canonical stacks by pullback and pushforward along the fibre product over the canonical stack of the contraction target, revisiting the local picture in Kawamata's work.
item.dc:creator: Xingbang Hao

item.title: Geometric Obstructions and Sharp Genus Dependence in LCD Scalings
item.description: arXiv:2611.04863v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the least pole order of a rational function whose nonzero evaluations scale a prescribed code to a Euclidean LCD code. A residue-one differential yields an obstruction for odd-dimensional one-point AG codes in characteristic two: for $C=C_L(D,aQ)$ with $0\le a<n$ and odd dimension, the threshold is at least $n+2g-a-1$. The obstruction uses alternating Gram matrices and does not require the scaled code to be self-orthogonal. For the dimension-three codes $C_L(D,(r+1)Q)$ on Hermitian curves over $\F_{r^2}$, $r=2^e\ge4$, we obtain \[ n+2g-r-2\le\tau_D(C;Q)\le n+2g-3. \] Consequently the leading genus contribution is asymptotically sharp even in dimension three. On the elliptic curve $y^2+y=x^3$ over $\F_4$, we prove the exact dimension-three threshold $6$ by an explicit multiplier. For repetition codes on the Hermitian family, the threshold equals the general interpolation bound $n+2g-1$. The upper bounds use information sets and hold for $q>3k$, and for $q>2k$ in characteristic two.
item.dc:creator: Rahim Rahmati-Asghar

item.title: Algebraic ellipticity of double covers of $(\mathbf P^1)^3$
item.description: arXiv:2611.04983v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that every smooth complex double cover of $(\mathbf P^1)^3$ branched along a smooth divisor of tridegree $(2,2,2)$ is algebraically Gromov elliptic. These irrational Fano threefolds form Mori--Mukai family 3-1 and have anticanonical genus seven and Picard rank three. Their three coordinate projections define degree-four del Pezzo fibrations. Each threefold also admits a dominant rational map of degree two from $\mathbf P^3$.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Dvorsky, Shulim Kaliman, Mikhail Zaidenberg

item.title: Projective symmetries of Chebyshev polynomials
item.description: arXiv:2611.05096v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field of odd characteristic $p$, and let $\varphi_d$ be the monic Chebyshev polynomial defined by $\varphi_d(t+t^{-1})=t^d+t^{-d}$. For $d>4$ with $p\nmid d$, let $H_d\le\text{PGL}_2(k)$ be the stabilizer of the zero set of $\varphi_d$. We show that \[ H_d\cong \begin{cases} D_d,&\text{if }2d=p^r+1\;\text{ for some integer }\;r\geq 1,\\ S_3,&\text{if }4d=p^r+1\;\text{ for some integer }\; r\geq 1,\\ C_2,&\text{otherwise}. \end{cases} \]
item.dc:creator: Saeed Tafazolian, Jaap Top

item.title: Relative cohomology and base-change
item.description: arXiv:2611.05209v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this note we prove a simple generalization of cohomology and base-change which seems to be missing from standard sources. We illustrate its usefulness by providing an alternative proof of a result of Ishimura on descent of vector bundles along blowups at a smooth center.
item.dc:creator: Andres Fernandez Herrero, Giovanni Inchiostro

item.title: On the $abc$ conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2611.05217v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Using adelic intersection theory and following the method envisioned by Parshin and Moret-Bailly, we prove a conjecture of Vojta for curves of genus two and a weak form of the $abc$ conjecture
item.dc:creator: Christophe Soul\'e

item.title: Gepner stability conditions on hypersurface categories
item.description: arXiv:2611.05350v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct numerical Bridgeland stability conditions on the category of graded matrix factorizations of every smooth complex projective hypersurface of degree $d\ge2$. These conditions are of Gepner type $(\tau,2/d)$, where $\tau$ is the grading shift autoequivalence. By Orlov's theorem, this gives stability conditions of Gepner type on all Calabi--Yau hypersurfaces and on Kuznetsov components of all Fano hypersurfaces. These conditions satisfy a mass-Hom bound and the support property on the full numerical Grothendieck group. Semistable objects of fixed numerical class and phase admit proper good moduli spaces.
item.dc:creator: Anibal Aravena, Peize Liu, Jenia Tevelev

item.title: Positive scalar curvature K\"ahler cones on compact complex surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2609.27870v2 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We determine the positive scalar curvature K\"ahler cone of every minimal compact K\"ahler surface of Kodaira dimension $-\infty$. By the Enriques--Kodaira classification, every such surface is either $\mathbb P^2$ or a geometrically ruled surface $\mathbb P(E)\to\Sigma_g$, where $E$ is a rank-two holomorphic vector bundle over a compact Riemann surface of genus $g$. On $\mathbb P^2$, every K\"ahler class admits a K\"ahler metric of positive scalar curvature, whereas on $\mathbb P(E)$, every K\"ahler class of positive total scalar curvature admits a metric of positive scalar curvature if and only if $g\le1$ or $E$ is slope-semistable. We further prove that if a smooth compact K\"ahler surface admits a birational morphism onto a ruled surface $\mathbb P(E)\to\Sigma_g$, where $g\ge2$ and $E$ is slope-unstable, then it contains a K\"ahler class of positive total scalar curvature admitting no positive scalar curvature K\"ahler metric. Finally, for every smooth compact K\"ahler surface $X$ birational to $Y=\mathbb P^2$ or $Y=\mathbb P(E)$, we show that K\"ahler classes admitting positive scalar curvature metrics on $Y$ are exactly the pushforwards of classes admitting such metrics on $X$.
item.dc:creator: Zehao Sha

item.title: Binomial Artin-Schelter Regular Algebras and Twisted Monoid Algebras
item.description: arXiv:2611.03989v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study four-dimensional binomial Artin-Schelter regular algebras and their connection with twisted monoid algebras. Starting with $23$ examples up to permutation of generators, we investigate the associated monoids of I-type and the structure of their groups of fractions. We determine the corresponding finite permutation groups and compute the second group cohomology $H^2(G(M),k^\times)$. These computations allow us to construct explicit families of four-dimensional Koszul Artin-Schelter regular algebras through cocycle twists. We illustrate this construction for some of these algebras.
item.dc:creator: Vishal Bhatoy

item.title: Rational points on loxodromic K3 surfaces and complex dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2611.04210v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We establish an analogue of the Hilbert irreducibility theorem for all K3 surfaces over number fields that admit an automorphism of positive entropy. Our method draws ingredients from both algebraic geometry and complex dynamics.
item.dc:creator: Dami\'an Gvirtz-Chen, Zhizhong Huang, Zhuchao Ji, Junyi Xie

item.title: Upper Bounds on the Strassen CP Rank Gap and Symmetric Rank Gap of Third-Order Tensors
item.description: arXiv:2611.04502v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For two third-order tensors over $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$, we define the Strassen CP rank gap as the sum of their CP ranks minus the CP rank of their direct sum. For arbitrary third-order tensors, we derive explicit upper bounds on this gap in terms of CP rank excess and dimension. For symmetric third-order tensors, we similarly define the Strassen symmetric rank gap using symmetric rank and establish explicit upper bounds in terms of symmetric rank excess, CP rank excess, and dimension. These bounds also yield sufficient conditions for the respective gaps to vanish, ensuring additivity of CP rank or symmetric rank under direct sums.
item.dc:creator: Jianze Li

item.title: Pseudo-Einstein Structures on Links of Isolated Singularities
item.description: arXiv:2611.04851v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study Jack Lee's conjecture that, for a compact strictly pseudoconvex CR manifold $M$, the condition $c_1(T^{1,0}M)=0$ in $H^2(M,\mathbb{R})$ implies the existence of a pseudo-Einstein structure. For links of isolated singularities, we construct counterexamples in every odd dimension at least three, with $c_1(T^{1,0}M)=0$ in $H^2(M,\mathbb{Z})$ and $b_1(M)=0$. For isolated algebraic singularities of log canonical type and complex dimension at least three, we prove that the real Chern class condition is equivalent to $\mathbb{Q}$-Cartierness of the canonical divisor, log canonicity, and the existence of a pseudo-Einstein structure. Finally, we construct a Du Bois threefold singularity whose link satisfies the real Chern class condition but admits no pseudo-Einstein structure. The initial versions of the proofs were generated with AI assistance and were subsequently revised and verified by the authors.
item.dc:creator: Yoshinori Gongyo, Kengo Hirachi, Shuya Matsumoto, Yuya Takeuchi

item.title: Boundary determination from the anisotropic elastic Dirichlet-to-Neumann map
item.description: arXiv:2611.04856v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We show that the Dirichlet-to-Neumann map of the elastic wave equation determines the density and the anisotropic stiffness tensor on the boundary for generic density and stiffness tensor fields. The proof builds on an interplay between microlocal analysis and algebraic geometry. Microlocal analysis yields a construction of special solutions, valid for many real principal type systems, that concentrate near a boundary point. Generic conditions ensure that this construction holds and allow for extraction of information about stiffness tensor and density at the boundary. We also describe the generic sets through algebraic conditions.
item.dc:creator: Joonas Ilmavirta, Mikko Salo, Hj{\o}rdis Schl\"uter, Daniel Windisch

item.title: On Douglas' conjecture for $m$-Kronecker quivers
item.description: arXiv:2611.04862v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove Douglas' conjecture for $m$-Kronecker quivers for each $m \geq 3$ on the normalized logarithms of Euler characteristics of moduli spaces. Also, we state a log-concavity conjecture on Euler characteristics near slope one for the 3-Kronecker quiver.
item.dc:creator: So Okada

item.title: Substantially Improved Rate and Distance for Addressable Transversal Phase Gates
item.description: arXiv:2611.04964v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: An important ingredient in fault-tolerant quantum computation is asymptotically good codes with fully addressable transversal non-Clifford gates. Existing constructions, however, provide only small explicit guarantees for rate and relative distance. Here, we substantially improve these guarantees for fully addressable transversal phase gates at every fixed level $h\ge3$ of the Clifford hierarchy, using a cyclic encoding beyond the binary CSS framework. The encoding separates logical phase control from the joint design of rate and distance, enabling two constructions with different computational costs. A deterministic polynomial-time algebraic-geometric construction gives a common asymptotic lower bound of $52/(675h)$ on both quantities. A counting argument gives an exponential-time construction with exact verification, improving this bound by a factor of approximately $2.86$. We further establish a universal upper bound for codes supporting fully addressable transversal single-qubit phase gates. Within our cyclic encoding framework, we obtain a stronger upper bound that is approximately $1.28$ times the lower bound achieved by our exponential-time construction. As concrete examples, we construct codes with $48$ and $90$ physical qubits supporting fully addressable transversal $T$ gates. These results narrow the gap between achievable code parameters and addressability bounds, providing quantitative targets for further improvements in efficient code constructions.
item.dc:creator: Bujiao Wu, Tongyin Lin, Bin Cheng

item.title: Algebraic $\mathbb{A}^{1}$-invariance of K-theory for affinoid Tate adic spaces of good reduction
item.description: arXiv:2611.05111v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We establish homotopy invariance for connective continuous K-theory of affinoid Tate adic spaces of good reduction with respect to the algebraic affine line, distinct from the adic affine line as analytic stacks. We approach this through an investigation of boundedness of t-structures on nuclear module categories, to which end we also study ultrasolid modules, a variant of solid modules, and their properties.
item.dc:creator: Hyungseop Kim

item.title: Mapping class group actions on the cohomology of configuration spaces of surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.05126v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let X be a closed oriented surface of genus at least 2 and P a finite subset of X. We bound the action of the mapping class group of (X,P) on the rational cohomology groups of the ordered configuration spaces F_n(X-P) of X-P. In particular, we show that, when #P < 2, the diagonal action of the mapping class group on the direct sum of the H^n(F_n(X-P)) is faithful, and determine its kernel when #P > 1.
item.dc:creator: Cl\'ement Dupont, Richard Hain

item.title: Two examples in amplituhedron tilings
item.description: arXiv:2611.05216v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We give an example of a tiling of the $m=4$ amplituhedron that has fewer cells than that of the magic number conjecture. The tiling uses an injective degree two cell.
item.dc:creator: Evgeniya Akhmedova, Thomas Lam, Calvin Yost-Wolff

item.title: Geometry of Spaces of Subrings
item.description: arXiv:2611.05370v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Motivated by examples such as the local rings of projective integral schemes and the Zariski-Riemann space of a field, we develop a geometry for continuously indexed families of subrings of a commutative ring $R$. The indexing spaces are Stone spaces, and continuity is taken with respect to the Zariski topology on the space of subrings. To each such family we associate a subsheaf of the constant sheaf with value $R$ whose stalks are the indexed subrings. This gives a patch ringed space. Its global sections are locally constant $R$-valued functions whose value at each point belongs to the corresponding subring. The ring of global sections, with this representation, is the associated patch algebra. Our main result establishes an algebra-geometry correspondence between these continuously indexed families of subrings and patch ringed spaces that can be expressed as a category equivalence, with each of the two categories dually equivalent to the category of patch algebras. Thus the indexing space, its sheaf, and the indexed subrings can be recovered functorially from the associated patch algebra, which serves as a coordinate ring for this geometry. We describe kernels and factorizations of patch algebra morphisms in geometric terms and characterize their injectivity and surjectivity. We include applications to Pierce duality and Bhatt-Scholze $w$-localizations of integral separated quasi-compact schemes.
item.dc:creator: Laura Cossu, Bruce Olberding, Giovanni Secreti

item.title: $P=W$ via $\mathcal{H}_2$
item.description: arXiv:2209.05429v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $\mathcal{H}_2$ be the Lie algebra of polynomial Hamiltonian vector fields on the symplectic plane. Let $X$ be the moduli space of stable Higgs bundles of fixed relatively prime rank and degree, or more generally the moduli space of stable parabolic Higgs bundles of arbitrary rank and degree for a generic stability condition. Let $H^*(X)$ be the cohomology with rational coefficients. Using the operations of cup-product by tautological classes and Hecke correspondences we construct an action of $\mathcal{H}_2$ on $H^*(X)[x,y]$, where $x$ and $y$ are formal variables. We show that the perverse filtration on $H^*(X)$ coincides with the filtration canonically associated to $\mathfrak{sl}_2\subset \mathcal{H}_2$ and deduce the $P=W$ conjecture of de Cataldo-Hausel-Migliorini.
item.dc:creator: Tamas Hausel, Anton Mellit, Alexandre Minets, Olivier Schiffmann

item.title: Fundamental groups, coregularity, and low dimensional klt Calabi-Yau pairs
item.description: arXiv:2401.01315v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this article, we study how the absolute coregularity of a projective log pair reflects on its fundamental group. More precisely, we conjecture that for a projective klt log pair $(X,D)$ of absolute coregularity $c$ (and arbitrary dimension) the fundamental group $\pi_1^{\rm reg}(X,D)$ admits a normal abelian subgroup of finite index and rank at most $2c$. We prove this conjecture in the cases $0 \leq c \leq 3$, building on the almost abelianity of the fundamental groups of klt Calabi-Yau pairs of dimension $\leq 3$. In the cases $c \in \{0,1,2\}$ and fixed dimension, we can furthermore bound the index of a solvable normal subgroup. In dimension three, we are able to prove almost abelianity of the fundamental group of the regular locus for projective klt Calabi-Yau pairs.
item.dc:creator: Lukas Braun, Fernando Figueroa

item.title: Conic Multiview Varieties
item.description: arXiv:2404.03063v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present an algebraic study of projections of conics in space onto multiple images of pinhole cameras. We study the Zariski closures of the projection images, which we call conic multiview varieties. Extending previous work for point and line multiview varieties, we use back-projected cones to describe these varieties. For two views, we determine the defining ideals of conic multiview varieties and describe their singular loci. For any number of views, we characterize when the simplest possible set-theoretic description is achieved based on the geometry of the camera centers. Finally, we investigate the complexity of the associated triangulation problem and conjecture the Euclidean distance degree for the conic multiview variety for two cameras.
item.dc:creator: Felix Rydell, Isak Sundelius

item.title: Anticanonical divisor with good asymptotic base loci
item.description: arXiv:2411.04628v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We characterize varieties of Fano type in terms of potentially log canonical pairs and birational Zariski decompositions. We also prove the existence of anticanonical minimal models of a potentially lc pair $(X,\Delta)$ under the assumptions that no potentially log canonical centers are contained in the augmented base locus of $-(K_X+\Delta)$ and that $-(K_X+\Delta)$ is a big $\mathbb{Q}$-Cartier divisor admitting a birational Zariski decomposition with NQC positive part. This can be considered as an anticanonical analogue of the results by Birkar--Hu.
item.dc:creator: Sung Rak Choi, Sungwook Jang, Dae-Won Lee

item.title: Cohomology of vector bundles on the moduli space of parabolic connections on $\mathbb{P}^1$ minus $5$ points
item.description: arXiv:2510.12578v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the moduli space of parabolic connections of rank two on the complex projective line $\mathbb{P}^1$ minus five points with fixed spectral data. We prove a cohomological vanishing theorem for tensor products of four natural vector bundles on the moduli stack of $\nu$-${\mathfrak sl}_2$-parabolic connections. We also compute the cohomology of the structure sheaf and give an explicit geometric description of a compactification of this moduli space, using $\epsilon$-connections and the birational geometry of $\mathbb{P}^2 \times (\mathbb{P}^2)^{\vee}$. As an application, we construct a universal family of twisted $D$-modules whose fibers satisfy an orthogonality property over a dense open subset. These results are motivated by Arinkin's approach to the tamely ramified geometric Langlands correspondence.
item.dc:creator: Yuki Matsubara

item.title: Hierarchical filtrations of vector bundles and birational geometry
item.description: arXiv:2512.18654v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study chains of locally free subsheaves of equal rank whose successive quotients are nonzero divisorial torsion sheaves. Fixing the determinant of the initial term defines a normalized hierarchical depth. An ample intersection argument proves finiteness on every smooth projective variety. On an algebraically closed smooth projective curve, the depth equals the degree of the determinant difference precisely when that difference is effective; otherwise, no normalized filtration exists. For birational morphisms of smooth projective surfaces, reflexive pushforward contracts exactly those steps whose determinant divisors are entirely exceptional. This yields a comparison of filtration lengths without a commutativity assumption. Explicit examples show that pullback can strictly increase depth and compute a depth of twenty on a two-point blowup. Finally, we distinguish preservation of evaluation codes for genuinely descended bundles from removal of zero coordinates caused by exceptional fixed components. The coding statements use specified compatible fiber bases or the block Hamming metric.
item.dc:creator: Rahim Rahmati-Asghar

item.title: Terminal Fano 4-fold Hypersurfaces via Deep Reinforcement Learning
item.description: arXiv:2603.15437v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We construct $46{,}992$ new families of Fano $4$-fold hypersurfaces $X_d\subset\mathbb(a_1,\ldots,a_6)$ of Fano index $1$ with $d>200$, whose general members have terminal singularities. Unlike the $11{,}617$ quasismooth families classified by Brown and Kasprzyk, these are nonquasismooth, for which determining terminality can require the analysis of hyperquotient singularities. An exhaustive search has classified all nonquasismooth families with $d\leq200$, but extending this classification to higher degrees becomes computationally prohibitive. We therefore exploit the sparsity and spatial clustering of terminal examples using two best-first searches over $\mathbb{Z}^6$: one with a fixed heuristic, and the other with a neural network trained online by deep reinforcement learning. Together, the searches reach degrees up to $3{,}234$. The neural network additionally discovers an average of $79$ hard-to-reach families per run. For the most isolated examples, our conservative distance-based model gives an estimated lower bound of nearly $40\%$ of the fixed search's total step budget to discover a single such family. An ablation study demonstrates that this advantage arises from the neural network rather than stochastic exploration alone. The complete list of families is publicly available.
item.dc:creator: Marc Truter

item.title: Reconstruction of F-cohomological field theories on moduli of compact type
item.description: arXiv:2604.07270v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove an analogue of Givental-Teleman reconstruction for F-cohomological field theories on the moduli space of compact type. We apply it to reconstruct the restriction of the extended $r$-spin classes to the extended direction and deduce relations between $\kappa$-classes (both in compact type).
item.dc:creator: Ga\"etan Borot, Silvia Ragni, Paolo Rossi

item.title: K-theory of Gieseker variety and type A cyclotomic Hecke algebra
item.description: arXiv:2605.11579v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We give an algebraic description of the equivariant K-theory of Gieseker varieties. Our main result identifies the equivariant K-theory of the Gieseker space with the Jucys--Murphy center of the cyclotomic Hecke algebra, over the equivariant K-theory of a point. The construction is inspired by the proof of the Hikita--Nakajima conjecture for Gieseker spaces given by the first and third authors. We discuss consequences for the center of cyclotomic Hecke algebras and for specializations to q=1 and to roots of unity. In particular, we relate K-theory of affine type A quiver varieties with the centers of the corresponding blocks of specialized cyclotomic Hecke algebras. This last result strengthens the correspondences obtained by the second author in earlier work.
item.dc:creator: Vasily Krylov, Rapha\"el Paegelow, Pavel Shlykov

item.title: Frobenius--Witt cotangent complexes
item.description: arXiv:2605.14803v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce the notion of the Frobenius--Witt cotangent complex, which can be considered as a derived variant of the module of Frobenius--Witt differentials defined by T. Saito. This new object also can be seen as an arithmetic variant of the notion of cotangent complex. We explain the suitability of these two viewpoints through a series of propositions. Furthermore, we establish a relationship between Frobenius--Witt cotangent complexes and the regularity of noetherian local rings, which can be considered as a derived variant of Saito's regularity criterion. This proof relies heavily on computations of Frobenius--Witt cotangent complexes in the case of perfectoid rings. We also study the deformation theory of delta structures using Frobenius--Witt cotangent complexes.
item.dc:creator: Kanau Shimada

item.title: On the Hodge and Tate conjectures for moduli spaces of curves
item.description: arXiv:2605.20453v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We survey recent progress on the cohomology of moduli spaces of stable curves through the lens of the Hodge and Tate conjectures, especially their generalized coniveau forms, which relate Hodge structures and l-adic Galois representations on cohomology to algebraic cycles. We explain how the inductive structure of the boundary stratification verifies these conjectures in a surprisingly wide range of cases, describe the guiding inspiration from arithmetic, and discuss open problems and directions for future research.
item.dc:creator: Sam Payne

item.title: Cellular $\mathbb{A}^1$-Homology from Bruhat Boundary Matrices of Split Semisimple Flag Varieties
item.description: arXiv:2607.02985v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We determine the cellular $\mathbb{A}^1$-chain complex of full and partial flag varieties of split semisimple simply connected groups over a perfect field of characteristic different from 2. With compatible integral normal orientations and reindexing by opposite Bruhat cells, the differential in each degree at least two is represented by the motivic Hopf map $\eta$ times one half of the signed cellular boundary matrix of the corresponding real flag manifold. Consequently, the Smith data of the resulting integer complex give all positive-degree cellular homology sheaves in terms of Milnor--Witt $K$-theory and the kernels and cokernels of integer multiples of $\eta$. We obtain a uniform computation of the second cellular $\mathbb{A}^1$-homology of $SL_n/B$ for $n\geq3$, together with complete calculations for $SL_3/B$ and the full flags of types $F_4$ and $G_2$.
item.dc:creator: Haoyang Liu, Tianle Liu

item.title: A note on prismatic sites for p-quasisyntomic rings
item.description: arXiv:2607.04931v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $p$ be a fixed prime number and let $R$ be a $p$-quasisyntomic ring. We provide conditions for objects in the absolute prismatic site $R_\Prism$ to cover the final object in $\Shv(R_\Prism)$ and to admit finite self-coproducts in $R_\Prism$. More precisely, we introduce in $R_\Prism$ the so-called transversal objects, so that the coproduct of any object in $R_\Prism$ with a transversal object exists in $R_\Prism$. As an immediate generalization, we introduce the so-called relatively quasiregular semiperfectoid covers of $R$, whose prismatic cohomology (of $\delta$-pairs, in the sense of Antieau-Krause-Nikolaus) produces objects in $R_\Prism$ that cover the final object in $\Shv(R_\Prism)$ and admit finite self-coproducts in $R_\Prism$.
item.dc:creator: Jingbang Guo

item.title: Flag Varieties of General Quiver Representations: Characteristic Classes and Semi-Invariants
item.description: arXiv:2607.12458v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study flags of subrepresentations of a general representation of a finite quiver. For each representation, its flag scheme is the zero scheme of a section of a quotient bundle on a product of partial flag varieties. We obtain the generic dimension and cycle class and equivariant localization formulas for Euler characteristics and parabolic Schubert coefficients. We further express these coefficients as finite signed sums of semi-invariant dimensions for auxiliary star quivers with inward and outward flag arms. In the acyclic one-step case, this is compatible with the result of Derksen--Schofield--Weyman, and the zero-dimensional case recovers their semi-invariant counting theorem. Examples treat matrix pencils and generalized Kronecker quivers.
item.dc:creator: Jiarui Fei

item.title: A Torelli-type theorem for hyperk\"{a}hler quotients
item.description: arXiv:2608.08680v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we investigate the moduli space of algebraic asymptotic hyperk\"{a}hler structures on hyperk\"{a}hler quotients arising from a quaternionic vector space $\mathbb{H}^n$. We consider the period map on this moduli space, and prove a Torelli-type theorem (i.e., the bijectivity of the period map) under mild assumptions including the surjectivity of the Kirwan map. This work provides an algebro-geometric generalization of the Torelli-type theorem for ALE gravitational instantons by Kronheimer (1989). In particular, this theorem applies to toric hyperk\"ahler varieties and Nakajima quiver varieties.
item.dc:creator: Ryota Kotani

item.title: Witt groups of smooth real curves and surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2608.18599v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the $\mathbf{I}^*$-cohomology of a smooth real algebraic curve in terms of its real locus and its geometric genus. We notably extend results of Knebusch and Monnier to the twisted case. We further describe how to compute twisted Witt groups of surfaces, generalising work of Sujatha, and apply our results to the computation of the shifted and twisted Witt groups of the smooth real anisotropic quadric surface. Finally, we extend Monnier's investigation of the image of the global signature homomorphism for surfaces.
item.dc:creator: Samuel Lerbet

item.title: On the Brill--Noether Theory of Sheaves on Regular Surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2609.06824v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the Brill--Noether theory of higher rank sheaves on surfaces $X$ with $H^1(X,\mathcal{O}_X) = 0$ and its interactions with the classical Brill--Noether theory of line bundles on curves lying on $X$. Denoting by $\mathrm{Spl}(v)$ the moduli space of simple sheaves on $X$ with Chern character $v = (r,c_1,\mathrm{ch}_2)$, we introduce the Brill--Noether loci $BN^k(v)^\circ \subseteq \mathrm{Spl}(v)$ of \emph{generically $k$-generated} sheaves and show, under assumptions on $c_1$ and $K_X$, certain well-behavedness results. In particular, if $c_1$ is \emph{indecomposable} and $X$ is a K3 surface, we generalize a Brill--Noether theorem for sheaves on K3s due to Yoshioka. This is achieved by employing He's deformation theory of the moduli space of coherent systems and a globalization of the Lazarsfeld--Mukai construction, providing a correspondence between the Brill--Noether theories of generically $r$-generated sheaves on $X$ and that of line bundles on curves $C \in |c_1|$. The same techniques yield upper bounds on the dimension of $\mathcal{W}^{r,\mathrm{bpf}}_d(|c_1|) \setminus \mathcal{W}^{r+1}_d(|c_1|)$ consisting of basepoint-free line bundles in terms of the number of endomorphisms of associated Lazarsfeld--Mukai bundles, for arbitrary $c_1$. This generalizes a result of Aprodu and Farkas in the context of Green's conjecture beyond K3 surfaces. In the case $r = 1$ of pencils, we obtain smoothness and expected-dimension results under an effectivity condition on $-K_X|_C$ for $C \in |c_1|$. As an application, we prove Green's conjecture for the general curve on a rational surface with a nef and effective anticanonical divisor.
item.dc:creator: Samir Geiger, Andreas Kretschmer

item.title: Universal Formulas for de Jonqui\`eres Loci and Equivariant Contact Problems
item.description: arXiv:2609.30892v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Given a family of genus $g$ curves $f:\Psi\to S$ and a relative degree $d$ line bundle $L$ on $\Psi$ such that $f_*L$ is a vector bundle, the projectivization $\mathbb{P}(f_*L)$ is stratified by relative de Jonqui\`eres loci, which parameterize sections of $L$ with prescribed vanishing orders. We give universal formulas for the classes of these loci in terms of the relative $O(1)$ on $\mathbb{P}(f_*L)$ and tautological classes pulled back from the universal Picard stack $\mathrm{Pic}_g^d$. When $f$ is the family of lines in $\mathbb{P}^r$, we use the universal polynomials to compute $\mathrm{GL}_{r+1}$-equivariant classes of loci of hypersurfaces and complete intersections admitting lines with prescribed contact orders.
item.dc:creator: Smita Rajan

item.title: The genus of a curve on Calabi-Yau threefolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.25065v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $X$ be a smooth projective Calabi-Yau variety of dimension $3$, with Picard number one. Let $n$ be the self-intersection of the ample generator of the N\'eron-Severi group of $X$. Let $\mathsf{GV}_{g,d}$ be the Gopakumar-Vafa invariant of $X$ of genus $g$ and degree $d$. It is conjectured that {\it if $g>\frac{d^{2}}{2n}+\frac{d}{2}+1$, then $\mathsf{GV}_{g,d}=0$}. In this paper, we prove the implication when $d\gg n$ and $X\subset \mathbb P^r$ is a complete intersection in projective space. The vanishing follows by proving that if $C$ is a closed subscheme of $X$ of dimension $1$, arithmetic genus $p_a(C)$, and degree $d\gg n$, then $p_a(C) \leq \frac{d^2}{2n}+\frac{d}{2}+1$. Actually, we prove a somewhat more general result. In particular, we prove that $C$ is an extremal curve if and only if $C$ is the complete intersection on $X$ with a hyperplane $H$ and a hypersurface $F$, namely $C=X\cap H\cap F$.
item.dc:creator: Vincenzo Di Gennaro, Antonio Rapagnetta, Pietro Sabatino

item.title: Parametrized Jacobian Problem over $\mathbb{C}^n$ and its Complete Resolution
item.description: arXiv:2610.35918v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We formulate a parametrized Jacobian Problem over $\mathbb{C}^{n}$ by incorporating independent scale parameters into the linear part of a polynomial map via polar decomposition. We prove that requiring the Jacobian determinant to remain constant uniformly across the parameter space decouples the Jacobian equation into a system enforcing the vanishing of all principal minors of the perturbation matrix. This system strictly forces lower triangularization up to variable permutations, establishing a necessary and sufficient condition for polynomial invertibility throughout the parameter family and providing an explicit, canonical scheme for constructing the inverse map in every dimension.
item.dc:creator: Yisong Yang

item.title: Dwork Motives, Monodromy and Potential Automorphy
item.description: arXiv:2407.16481v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper we study certain families of motives, which arise as direct summands of the cohomology of the Dwork family. We computationally find examples of interesting families with the following three properties. Firstly, their geometric monodromy group is Zariski dense in $\operatorname{SL}_n$. Secondly, they realise many different unipotent operators as the monodromy operator at $t = \infty$. Thirdly, all their Hodge numbers are $\leq 1$. This has consequences for Galois representations. Namely, if a nilpotent operator $N$ appears as the monodromy at $t = \infty$ in one of our families, we can construct potentially automorphic representations with $\ell$-adic monodromy given by $N$ at a fixed prime $p$. As another application, we obtain a new proof of some cases of the recent local-global compatibility theorem of Matsumoto.
item.dc:creator: Lambert A'Campo

item.title: Skein and cluster algebras of punctured surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2503.15037v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove the full Fock--Goncharov conjecture for the $\mathcal{A}_{SL_2,\Sigma_{g,p}}$-cluster variety associated with the moduli space of decorated twisted $SL_2$-local systems on triangulable surfaces $\Sigma_{g,p}$ with at least two punctures. Equivalently, we show that the tagged skein algebra $Sk^{ta}(\Sigma)$, identified with the middle cluster algebra $\mathrm{mid}(\mathcal{A})$, coincides with the upper cluster algebra $U(\Sigma)$. Inspired by the work of Shen--Sun--Weng, we introduce a localized cluster variety $\mathring{\mathcal{A}}$ whose positive real locus is the decorated Teichm\"uller space $\mathcal{T}^d(\Sigma)$. For $p\geq2$, its ring of global sections is the normalization of the classical Roger--Yang skein algebra $Sk^{RY}_{q\to1}(\Sigma)$ and equals that algebra except for the four-punctured sphere. In the equality cases, the quantum Roger--Yang skein algebra $Sk^{RY}_q(\Sigma)$ provides a quantization of this global-section ring. We prove normality of $Sk^{ta}(\Sigma)$ for $p\geq2$, complementing its known Gorenstein property, and normality of $Sk^{RY}_{q\to1}(\Sigma)$ for every triangulable $\Sigma_{g,p}$ other than $\Sigma_{0,4}$. We also prove finite generation of $U(\Sigma_{g,p})$ for every triangulable $\Sigma_{g,p}$, including the once-punctured case.
item.dc:creator: Enhan Li

item.title: On Shilov boundaries, Rees valuations and integral extensions
item.description: arXiv:2507.07091v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We explore an analogy between, on one hand, the notions of integral closure of ideals and Rees valuations in commutative algebra and, on the other hand, the notions of spectral seminorm and Shilov boundary in nonarchimedean geometry. For any Tate ring $\mathcal{A}$ with a Noetherian ring of definition $\mathcal{A}_{0}$ and pseudo-uniformizer $\varpi\in\mathcal{A}_{0}$, we prove that the Shilov boundary for $\mathcal{A}$ naturally coincides with the set of Rees valuation rings of the principal ideal $(\varpi)_{\mathcal{A}_{0}}$ of $\mathcal{A}_{0}$. Furthermore, we characterize the Shilov boundary for a wide class of Tate rings by means of minimal open prime ideals in the subring of power-bounded elements. For affinoid algebras, in the sense of Tate, whose underlying rings are integral domains, this recovers a well-known result of Berkovich. Moreover, under some mild assumptions, we prove stability of our characterization of the Shilov boundary under (completed) integral extensions. In particular, for every mixed-characteristic Noetherian domain $R$, we obtain a description of the Shilov boundary for the Tate ring $\widehat{R^{+}}[p^{-1}]$, where $\widehat{R^{+}}$ is the $p$-adic completion of the absolute integral closure of the domain $R$.
item.dc:creator: Dimitri Dine

item.title: The $\mathrm{al}_{ab}$ functions of hyperelliptic curves: a generalization of Jacobi's elliptic functions and explicit solutions of a degenerate Krichever-Novikov equation
item.description: arXiv:2603.10386v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The Jacobi elliptic functions $\mathrm{sn}$, $\mathrm{cn}$, $\mathrm{dn}$ and their ratios are expressed by Weierstrass's functions $\mathrm{al}_a=\sqrt{x-b_a}$ of an elliptic curve. For a hyperelliptic curve of genus $g$, Weierstrass's $\mathrm{al}_a$ functions generalize $\mathrm{sn}$, $\mathrm{cn}$ and $\mathrm{dn}$, and the modified Korteweg-de Vries and sine-Gordon equations stand behind them. In this paper we study the $\mathrm{al}_{ab}$ functions, which are defined by the sigma function shifted by the sum of two half-periods and which, together with the ratios of the $\mathrm{al}_a$ functions, generalize the remaining Jacobi elliptic functions. We determine the exact lattice of periods of $\mathrm{al}_{12}$ and show that it is single-valued on the unramified double covering of the Jacobian corresponding to the double covering $\hat{w}^2=(x-b_1)(x-b_2)$ of the curve. We show that $\mathrm{al}_{12}$ is the Wronskian of the band-edge eigenfunctions $\mathrm{al}_1$ and $\mathrm{al}_2$, so that the half-period translations realize Darboux transformations. As the main result, $\mathrm{al}_{12}$, $\mathrm{al}_2/\mathrm{al}_1$ and $1/\mathrm{al}_{12}$ satisfy one and the same degenerate Krichever-Novikov equation, whose polynomial has the double roots $0$ and $\infty$, and the half-periods act on these solutions as the M\"obius symmetries of the equation. Thus the Krichever-Novikov equation stands behind the $\mathrm{al}_{ab}$ functions. In genus one these functions reduce to $\mathrm{sn}$, $\mathrm{ns}$ and $\mathrm{dc}$.
item.dc:creator: Shigeki Matsutani

item.title: Quadratic Complexity of Voronoi Diagrams in $\mathbb{R}^3$ for Lines in a Single Ruling of a Regulus
item.description: arXiv:2608.27114v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study nearest and farthest Voronoi diagrams of lines in three-dimensional Euclidean space, which partition space according to the closest and farthest input lines, respectively. For arbitrary lines, a gap remains between the known quadratic lower bound and near-cubic upper bounds for the complexity of the nearest diagram. We consider input lines chosen from one of two continuous families of straight lines on a smooth surface defined by a quadratic equation, with one line from each family passing through every point of the surface. Under the geometric assumptions stated in the paper, we prove quadratic upper bounds on the total number of vertices, edges, faces, and connected three-dimensional regions in both diagrams. We also construct quadratically many nearest vertices using lines from a single family on one fixed surface, establishing a tight quadratic worst-case bound. The farthest diagram has quadratic total complexity for every input satisfying our assumptions. Our proof uses a parametrization that arranges the input lines in a cyclic order and expresses tangency to a sphere by a polynomial equation of degree four. At a Voronoi vertex, the four tangent input lines give four distinct roots. The sign changes between these roots, together with the nearest or farthest condition, force two intervening parameter intervals to contain no other input parameters. Thus, only quadratically many choices of four lines can define a vertex, and each choice yields at most eight isolated candidate centers.
item.dc:creator: Eunku Park, Kangjin Han
